anomalies.observed: The LM1117-5.0 regulator U2 has both its input (VI) and its output (VO) tied to the +5V arrow; the raw supply net VCC is not connected to the regulator at all (its decoupling cap C2 sits on VCC, while C3 sits on +5V).
anomalies.expected: A linear regulator's input must be fed from the unregulated supply: VI should be on VCC (the fan/PMOS source rail) and VO should be the regulated +5V rail, so that the ATtiny and logic powered from +5V are derived from the board input.

evidence.quote: U2 LM1117-5.0: VI pin wire to '+5V', VO pin wire to '+5V'; C3 100nF on +5V, C2 100nF on VCC (right-hand sheet, top)

anomalies.impact: The +5V logic rail is never generated from the supply; the MCU and gate-driver logic will not power up (or, if VCC is a higher fan voltage, +5V is left floating), making the board non-functional.

anomalies.observed: NET0007 (the MCU XTAL2/PB4 pin) is pulled up to VCC through R2 (10K) and simultaneously to +5V through R8 (10K), joining two different supply rails onto a signal net that connects directly to the microcontroller pin.
anomalies.expected: A pull-up on a 5V MCU pin should reference only the 5V rail; tying the same node to the unregulated VCC rail over-voltages the pin and fights the +5V pull-up whenever VCC != +5V.

evidence.quote: R2 10K between VCC and NET0007; R8 10K between +5V and NET0007; U4 pin3 XTAL2/PB4 -> NET0007
Where it is silent, judge the design with standard electrical-engineering practice

anomalies.impact: If VCC is the fan supply (higher than 5V, as implied by the 5V1 clamp D2 on the gate-drive net), PB4 is driven above its supply and may be damaged, and the two pull-ups form a VCC-to-+5V current path.

anomalies.observed: The potentiometer J1 low-side pin (3) carries a GND arrow yet is also wired to NET0012, which continues to NET0007 (the VCC/+5V-pulled MCU PB4/RESET-related net).
anomalies.expected: J1 pin 3 should connect to GND only, so the pot forms a clean divider between +5V (pin 1) and ground with the wiper (pin 2 = NET0005) read by the ADC.

evidence.quote: J1 POT pin3 -> GND arrow and -> NET0012 -> NET0007 (root sheet, near J1/R8/R2)

anomalies.impact: The pot's ground reference is replaced by a pulled-up signal net, corrupting the speed-setpoint ADC reading and shorting GND to NET0012/NET0007.

parsed.summary: The build shows the 5V regulator U2 wired with its input tied to its own +5V output instead of the unregulated VCC supply (and the decoupling caps swapped), so the logic 5V rail is not derived from the input; the same VCC/+5V rails are additionally cross-connected through R2/R8 on the MCU PB4 net and the pot's ground pin, indicating mis-routed supply connections rather than a working ATtiny fan controller.
